theorems.name: transition_total
theorems.doc: No command panics, on any state.
theorems.statement: theorem transition_total (s : Queue) (c : Command) : ∃ r, transition s c = ok r
theorems.proof:
theorem transition_total (s : Queue) (c : Command) : ∃ r, transition s c = ok r := by
  have h : transition s c ⦃ _ => True ⦄ := by
    unfold transition
    cases c <;> h5i_steps
  exact H5iAppLib.ok_of h

theorems.name: inv_reachable
theorems.doc: In every reachable scheduler state — after any sequence of commands, successful or refused — the next poll is scheduled within 30 s.
theorems.statement:
theorem inv_reachable {st : Queue} {evs : List (H5iAppLib.Event Unit Command Reply Error)}
    (h : H5iAppLib.Run tr (id : Queue → Queue) applyW INIT st evs) : Inv st

theorems.name: enqueue_keeps_others
theorems.doc: Enqueuing one kind never evicts another: every other kind's pending state is unchanged. A scheduled Stop therefore survives any later poll scheduling.
theorems.statement:
theorem enqueue_keeps_others (q : Queue) (k : Kind) (time : U64) (replace : Bool) (k' : Kind)
    (hne : k' ≠ k) (n : Queue) (h : enqueue q k time replace = ok n) :
    slot n k' = slot q k'
theorems.proof:
theorem enqueue_keeps_others (q : Queue) (k : Kind) (time : U64) (replace : Bool) (k' : Kind)
    (hne : k' ≠ k) (n : Queue) (h : enqueue q k time replace = ok n) :
    slot n k' = slot q k' := by
  unfold enqueue at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o, -, h⟩ := h
  cases o with
  | none =>
    simp only at h
    rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h; obtain ⟨n1, h1, h⟩ := h
    rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h; obtain ⟨i, -, h⟩ := h
    rw [slot_with_pos n1 k i n h k']
    exact slot_with_slot_ne q k k' _ hne n1 h1
  | some e =>
    simp only at h
    rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h; obtain ⟨v, -, h⟩ := h
    exact slot_with_slot_ne q k k' (some v) hne n h

theorems.name: enqueue_never_delays
theorems.doc: A `PreferEarlier` re-enqueue never *delays* a command already pending: if `k` was due at `e`, after the enqueue it is due at some time `≤ e`. So re-scheduling a Stop can only move it earlier, never later.
theorems.statement:
theorem enqueue_never_delays (q : Queue) (k : Kind) (time e : U64) (n : Queue)
    (hpre : slot q k = ok (some e)) (h : enqueue q k time false = ok n) :
    ∃ t, slot n k = ok (some t) ∧ t.val ≤ e.val
theorems.proof:
theorem enqueue_never_delays (q : Queue) (k : Kind) (time e : U64) (n : Queue)
    (hpre : slot q k = ok (some e)) (h : enqueue q k time false = ok n) :
    ∃ t, slot n k = ok (some t) ∧ t.val ≤ e.val := by
  unfold enqueue at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o, ho, h⟩ := h
  rw [hpre] at ho
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at ho
  subst ho
  simp only at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨v, hv, h⟩ := h
  refine ⟨v, slot_with_slot_eq q k (some v) n h, ?_⟩
  simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at hv
  split at hv <;> (simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at hv; subst hv) <;> scalar_tac

theorems.name: pop_clears
theorems.doc: A popped event's slot is cleared: after `pop_due` returns a kind, that kind is no longer pending, so the same scheduled event is never executed twice.
theorems.statement:
theorem pop_clears (q : Queue) (now : U64) (n : Queue) (k : Kind)
    (h : pop_due q now = ok (n, some k)) : slot n k = ok none
theorems.proof:
theorem pop_clears (q : Queue) (now : U64) (n : Queue) (k : Kind)
    (h : pop_due q now = ok (n, some k)) : slot n k = ok none := by
  unfold pop_due at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o, -, h⟩ := h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o1, -, h⟩ := h
  cases o1 with
  | none => simp at h
  | some k' =>
    simp only at h
    rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
    obtain ⟨q1, hq1, h⟩ := h
    simp only [Result.ok.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at h
    obtain ⟨hn, hk⟩ := h
    rw [← hn, ← hk]
    exact (remove_slots q k' q1 hq1).1

theorems.name: pop_keeps_others
theorems.doc: Popping one event leaves every other pending event pending, at its time.
theorems.statement:
theorem pop_keeps_others (q : Queue) (now : U64) (n : Queue) (k k' : Kind) (hne : k' ≠ k)
    (h : pop_due q now = ok (n, some k)) : slot n k' = slot q k'
theorems.proof:
theorem pop_keeps_others (q : Queue) (now : U64) (n : Queue) (k k' : Kind) (hne : k' ≠ k)
    (h : pop_due q now = ok (n, some k)) : slot n k' = slot q k' := by
  unfold pop_due at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o, -, h⟩ := h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨o1, -, h⟩ := h
  cases o1 with
  | none => simp at h
  | some k1 =>
    simp only at h
    rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
    obtain ⟨q1, hq1, h⟩ := h
    simp only [Result.ok.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at h
    obtain ⟨hn, hk⟩ := h
    rw [← hn]
    rw [← hk] at hne
    exact (remove_slots q k1 q1 hq1).2 k' hne

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scheduler: user commands preempt polls at equal time (S).
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------

theorems.name: ties_follow_vector_order
theorems.doc: Two polls due at the same instant (same priority) pop in upstream's vector order: the one at the lower index first — `soonest_index`'s `min_by` keeps the first of equal elements.
theorems.statement:
theorem ties_follow_vector_order (t now : U64) (ht : t.val ≤ now.val) :
    pop_due
      { status := some t, cook := some t, recipes := none,
        start := none, stop := none, next := none,
        status_pos := 1#u8, cook_pos := 0#u8, recipes_pos := 0#u8,
        start_pos := 0#u8, stop_pos := 0#u8, next_pos := 0#u8, fail_count := 0#u64 } now
      ⦃ res => res.2 = some Kind.PollCurrentCook ⦄
theorems.proof:
theorem ties_follow_vector_order (t now : U64) (ht : t.val ≤ now.val) :
    pop_due
      { status := some t, cook := some t, recipes := none,
        start := none, stop := none, next := none,
        status_pos := 1#u8, cook_pos := 0#u8, recipes_pos := 0#u8,
        start_pos := 0#u8, stop_pos := 0#u8, next_pos := 0#u8, fail_count := 0#u64 } now
      ⦃ res => res.2 = some Kind.PollCurrentCook ⦄ := by
  have hnd : ¬ (t > now) := by scalar_tac
  unfold pop_due kind_of soonest_due consider better priority
  simp only [hnd, if_false, gt_iff_lt]
  simp
  step*

theorems.name: fill_hole_moves_last
theorems.doc: `swap_remove`'s move: a pending kind at the last index takes the freed index `p`; nothing else moves.
theorems.statement:
theorem fill_hole_moves_last (q : Queue) (j : Kind) (last p : U8) (n : Queue) (t : U64)
    (hj : slot q j = ok (some t)) (hl : pos q j = ok last)
    (h : fill_hole q j last p = ok n) : pos n j = ok p
theorems.proof:
theorem fill_hole_moves_last (q : Queue) (j : Kind) (last p : U8) (n : Queue) (t : U64)
    (hj : slot q j = ok (some t)) (hl : pos q j = ok last)
    (h : fill_hole q j last p = ok n) : pos n j = ok p := by
  unfold fill_hole at h
  simp [hj, hl] at h
  unfold with_pos at h
  cases j <;> (simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at h; subst h) <;> (unfold pos; simp)

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Failure count: counted exactly, as upstream reports it (C).
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------

theorems.name: poll_fail_counts
theorems.doc: A failed poll counts one more consecutive failure (until `u64::MAX`), so `/health` and the display show upstream's count, not one capped at a tier.
theorems.statement:
theorem poll_fail_counts (s n : Queue) (r : Reply) (hs : s.fail_count.val < U64.max)
    (h : transition s Command.PollFail = ok (.Ok (some n, r))) :
    n.fail_count.val = s.fail_count.val + 1
theorems.proof:
theorem poll_fail_counts (s n : Queue) (r : Reply) (hs : s.fail_count.val < U64.max)
    (h : transition s Command.PollFail = ok (.Ok (some n, r))) :
    n.fail_count.val = s.fail_count.val + 1 := by
  unfold transition at h
  have hne : s.fail_count ≠ core.num.U64.MAX := by
    intro he; rw [he] at hs; simp [core.num.U64.MAX, U64.max_eq, U64.rMax] at hs
  unfold incr_sat at h
  simp only [hne, if_false] at h
  rw [H5iAppLib.bind_eq_ok] at h
  obtain ⟨v, hv, h⟩ := h
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq, core.result.Result.Ok.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨rfl, -⟩ := h
  have h2 := UScalar.add_equiv s.fail_count 1#u64
  rw [hv] at h2
  obtain ⟨-, h3, -⟩ := h2
  show v.val = s.fail_count.val + 1
  rw [h3]; simp

-- Reset classification precedence (S) and round-trip (C).
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------

theorems.name: user_preempts_poll
theorems.doc: A representative preemption: a status poll and a Stop both due at the same instant `t`, the poll first in the vector — the Stop still pops first. The `user_loses_priority` mutant (swapping the tie-break) makes this pop the poll.
theorems.statement:
theorem user_preempts_poll (t now : U64) (ht : t.val ≤ now.val) :
    pop_due
      { status := some t, cook := none, recipes := none,
        start := none, stop := some t, next := none,
        status_pos := 0#u8, cook_pos := 0#u8, recipes_pos := 0#u8,
        start_pos := 0#u8, stop_pos := 1#u8, next_pos := 0#u8, fail_count := 0#u64 } now
      ⦃ res => res.2 = some Kind.UserStop ⦄
theorems.proof:
theorem user_preempts_poll (t now : U64) (ht : t.val ≤ now.val) :
    pop_due
      { status := some t, cook := none, recipes := none,
        start := none, stop := some t, next := none,
        status_pos := 0#u8, cook_pos := 0#u8, recipes_pos := 0#u8,
        start_pos := 0#u8, stop_pos := 1#u8, next_pos := 0#u8, fail_count := 0#u64 } now
      ⦃ res => res.2 = some Kind.UserStop ⦄ := by
  have hnd : ¬ (t > now) := by scalar_tac
  unfold pop_due kind_of soonest_due consider better priority
  simp only [hnd, if_false, gt_iff_lt]
  simp
  step*

theorems.name: poll_ok_recovers
theorems.doc: A single successful poll clears the failure count, so the device leaves the offline/backoff regime immediately: not offline, and polling at the 1 s rate.
theorems.statement:
theorem poll_ok_recovers (s : Queue) (n : Queue) (r : Reply)
    (h : transition s Command.PollOk = ok (.Ok (some n, r))) :
    n.fail_count.val = 0 ∧ is_offline n.fail_count = ok false ∧
      next_poll_interval n.fail_count = ok 1#u64
theorems.proof:
theorem poll_ok_recovers (s : Queue) (n : Queue) (r : Reply)
    (h : transition s Command.PollOk = ok (.Ok (some n, r))) :
    n.fail_count.val = 0 ∧ is_offline n.fail_count = ok false ∧
      next_poll_interval n.fail_count = ok 1#u64 := by
  unfold transition at h
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq, core.result.Result.Ok.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq,
    Option.some.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨rfl, -⟩ := h
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
  · unfold is_offline; simp [OFFLINE_THRESHOLD]
  · unfold next_poll_interval
    simp [TIER1_FAILS, TIER2_FAILS, TIER3_FAILS, NORMAL_POLL_SECS]

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scheduler: no eviction, kind retained (S).
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------

theorems.name: backoff_bounded
theorems.doc: The next poll is always scheduled between 1 and 30 seconds out: the backoff is bounded, so a failing device keeps retrying and never abandons the server.
theorems.statement:
theorem backoff_bounded (fc : U64) :
    next_poll_interval fc ⦃ r => 1 ≤ r.val ∧ r.val ≤ 30 ⦄
theorems.proof:
theorem backoff_bounded (fc : U64) :
    next_poll_interval fc ⦃ r => 1 ≤ r.val ∧ r.val ≤ 30 ⦄ := by
  unfold next_poll_interval
  split_ifs <;>
    simp [TIER1_SECS, TIER2_SECS, TIER3_SECS, NORMAL_POLL_SECS]

theorems.name: backoff_monotone
theorems.doc: More consecutive failures never shorten the poll interval.
theorems.statement:
theorem backoff_monotone (a b : U64) (hab : a.val ≤ b.val)
    (ra rb : U64) (ha : next_poll_interval a = ok ra) (hb : next_poll_interval b = ok rb) :
    ra.val ≤ rb.val
theorems.proof:
theorem backoff_monotone (a b : U64) (hab : a.val ≤ b.val)
    (ra rb : U64) (ha : next_poll_interval a = ok ra) (hb : next_poll_interval b = ok rb) :
    ra.val ≤ rb.val := by
  unfold next_poll_interval at ha hb
  simp only [TIER1_FAILS, TIER2_FAILS, TIER3_FAILS, TIER1_SECS, TIER2_SECS, TIER3_SECS,
    NORMAL_POLL_SECS, ge_iff_le, UScalar.le_equiv] at ha hb
  split_ifs at ha <;> split_ifs at hb <;>
    simp_all <;> scalar_tac

-- Poll health recovery (S).
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------

theorems.name: panic_never_masked
theorems.doc: A panic is attributed to the panic even when the watchdog also fired: the root cause is never masked as a plain watchdog timeout.
theorems.statement:
theorem panic_never_masked (las : U32) (wt wf : Bool) :
    classify_reset true true las wt wf = ok ResetReason.Panic
theorems.proof:
theorem panic_never_masked (las : U32) (wt wf : Bool) :
    classify_reset true true las wt wf = ok ResetReason.Panic := by
  unfold classify_reset; simp

theorems.name: coldboot_dominates
theorems.doc: With RAM lost (invalid magic) the boot is always a cold boot, whatever the other breadcrumbs say.
theorems.statement:
theorem coldboot_dominates (pa : Bool) (las : U32) (wt wf : Bool) :
    classify_reset false pa las wt wf = ok ResetReason.ColdBoot
theorems.proof:
theorem coldboot_dominates (pa : Bool) (las : U32) (wt wf : Bool) :
    classify_reset false pa las wt wf = ok ResetReason.ColdBoot := by
  unfold classify_reset; simp

theorems.name: sound
theorems.doc: Every accepted read-only command writes nothing, for all states.
theorems.statement:
theorem sound (s : Queue) (c : Command) (ws : Option Queue) (r : Reply)
    (hro : read_only c = ok true) (ht : transition s c = ok (.Ok (ws, r))) : ws = none
theorems.proof:
theorem sound (s : Queue) (c : Command) (ws : Option Queue) (r : Reply)
    (hro : read_only c = ok true) (ht : transition s c = ok (.Ok (ws, r))) : ws = none := by
  cases c <;> simp [read_only] at hro
  unfold transition at ht
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := H5iAppLib.ok_of (Proofs.next_poll_interval_spec s.fail_count)
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := H5iAppLib.ok_of (Proofs.is_offline_spec s.fail_count)
  simp [hi, hb] at ht
  exact ht.1.symm

remove.lean:
def remove (q : Queue) (k : Kind) : Result Queue := do
  let p ← pos q k
  let c ← pending_count q
  let last ← if c = 0#u8
               then ok 0#u8
               else c - 1#u8
  let n0 ← with_slot q k none
  let n1 ← fill_hole n0 Kind.PollStatus last p
  let n2 ← fill_hole n1 Kind.PollCurrentCook last p
  let n3 ← fill_hole n2 Kind.PollRecipes last p
  let n4 ← fill_hole n3 Kind.UserStart last p
  let n5 ← fill_hole n4 Kind.UserStop last p
  fill_hole n5 Kind.UserNextStage last p

transition.lean:
def transition
  (s : Queue) (cmd : Command) :
  Result (core.result.Result ((Option Queue) × Reply) Error)
  := do
  match cmd with
  | Command.Enqueue kind time replace =>
    let n ← enqueue s kind time replace
    ok (core.result.Result.Ok (some n, Reply.Queued))
  | Command.PopDue now =>
    let (n, popped) ← pop_due s now
    ok (core.result.Result.Ok (some n, Reply.Popped popped))
  | Command.PollOk =>
    ok (core.result.Result.Ok (some { s with fail_count := 0#u64 },
      Reply.Queued))
  | Command.PollFail =>
    let i ← incr_sat s.fail_count
    ok (core.result.Result.Ok (some { s with fail_count := i }, Reply.Queued))
  | Command.Peek =>
    let i ← next_poll_interval s.fail_count
    let b ← is_offline s.fail_count
    ok (core.result.Result.Ok (none, Reply.Health s.fail_count i b))
transition.upstream_note: dispatches to enqueue/pop_due and the record_fast_poll_success/failure fail_count updates

consider.lean:
def consider
  (best : Option (Std.U64 × Kind × Std.U8)) (s : Option Std.U64) (k : Kind)
  (p : Std.U8) (now : Std.U64) :
  Result (Option (Std.U64 × Kind × Std.U8))
  := do
  match s with
  | none => ok best
  | some t =>
    if t > now
    then ok best
    else
      match best with
      | none => ok (some (t, k, p))
      | some b =>
        let (i, k1, i1) := b
        let b1 ← better t k p i k1 i1
        if b1
        then ok (some (t, k, p))
        else ok best
consider.upstream_note: one fold step of soonest_index's min_by, filtered by pop_due's due check

fill_hole.lean:
def fill_hole
  (q : Queue) (j : Kind) (last : Std.U8) (p : Std.U8) : Result Queue := do
  let o ← slot q j
  match o with
  | none => ok q
  | some _ => let i ← pos q j
              if i = last
              then with_pos q j p
              else ok q

def pop_due (q : Queue) (now : Std.U64) : Result (Queue × (Option Kind)) := do
  let o ← soonest_due q now
  let o1 ← kind_of o
  match o1 with
  | none => ok (q, none)
  | some k => let q1 ← remove q k
              ok (q1, o1)

soonest_due.lean:
def soonest_due
  (q : Queue) (now : Std.U64) :
  Result (Option (Std.U64 × Kind × Std.U8))
  := do
  let b0 ← consider none q.status Kind.PollStatus q.status_pos now
  let b1 ← consider b0 q.cook Kind.PollCurrentCook q.cook_pos now
  let b2 ← consider b1 q.recipes Kind.PollRecipes q.recipes_pos now
  let b3 ← consider b2 q.start Kind.UserStart q.start_pos now
  let b4 ← consider b3 q.stop Kind.UserStop q.stop_pos now
  consider b4 q.next Kind.UserNextStage q.next_pos now
soonest_due.upstream_note: soonest_index plus pop_due's execution_time <= now check

read_only.lean:
def read_only (cmd : Command) : Result Bool := do
  match cmd with
  | Command.Enqueue _ _ _ => ok false
  | Command.PopDue _ => ok false
  | Command.PollOk => ok false
  | Command.PollFail => ok false
  | Command.Peek => ok true

is_offline.lean:
def is_offline (fail_count : Std.U64) : Result Bool := do
  ok (fail_count >= OFFLINE_THRESHOLD)

slot.lean:
def slot (q : Queue) (k : Kind) : Result (Option Std.U64) := do
  match k with
  | Kind.PollStatus => ok q.status
  | Kind.PollCurrentCook => ok q.cook
  | Kind.PollRecipes => ok q.recipes
  | Kind.UserStart => ok q.start
  | Kind.UserStop => ok q.stop
  | Kind.UserNextStage => ok q.next
slot.upstream_note: port-only accessor of the per-kind slot record; replaces events.iter().find(kind) lookup

is_init_stage.lean:
def is_init_stage (s : Std.U32) : Result Bool := do
  if s = INIT_STAGE_WIFI
  then ok true
  else ok (s = INIT_STAGE_DHCP)

better.lean:
def better
  (ct : Std.U64) (ck : Kind) (cp : Std.U8) (bt : Std.U64) (bk : Kind)
  (bp : Std.U8) :
  Result Bool
  := do
  if ct < bt
  then ok true
  else
    if ct > bt
    then ok false
    else
      let i ← priority ck
      let i1 ← priority bk
      if i < i1
      then ok true
      else if i > i1
           then ok false
           else ok (cp < bp)
better.upstream_note: the (execution_time, priority) comparator of soonest_index's min_by, with first-in-vector tie-break

upstream.code: pub const INIT_STAGE_WIFI: u32 = 100;

classify_reset.lean:
def classify_reset
  (magic_was_valid : Bool) (panic_count_advanced : Bool)
  (last_app_state : Std.U32) (watchdog_timer : Bool) (watchdog_force : Bool) :
  Result ResetReason
  := do
  if magic_was_valid
  then
    if panic_count_advanced
    then ok ResetReason.Panic
    else
      if watchdog_timer
      then ok ResetReason.WatchdogTimeout
      else
        if watchdog_force
        then ok ResetReason.WatchdogForced
        else
          let b ← is_init_stage last_app_state
          if b
          then ok ResetReason.InitTimeout
          else ok ResetReason.OtherSoftReset
  else ok ResetReason.ColdBoot

next_poll_interval.lean:
def next_poll_interval (fail_count : Std.U64) : Result Std.U64 := do
  if fail_count >= TIER3_FAILS
  then ok TIER3_SECS
  else
    if fail_count >= TIER2_FAILS
    then ok TIER2_SECS
    else
      if fail_count >= TIER1_FAILS
      then ok TIER1_SECS
      else ok NORMAL_POLL_SECS
next_poll_interval.upstream_note: ApiRuntime::next_poll_interval_secs, taking fail_count as an argument

pending_count.lean:
def pending_count (q : Queue) : Result Std.U8 := do
  let a ← bit q.status
  let i ← bit q.cook
  let b ← a + i
  let i1 ← bit q.recipes
  let c ← b + i1
  let i2 ← bit q.start
  let d ← c + i2
  let i3 ← bit q.stop
  let e ← d + i3
  let i4 ← bit q.next
  e + i4

enqueue.lean:
def enqueue
  (q : Queue) (k : Kind) (time : Std.U64) (replace : Bool) : Result Queue := do
  let o ← slot q k
  match o with
  | none =>
    let n ← with_slot q k (some time)
    let i ← pending_count q
    with_pos n k i
  | some existing =>
    let v ←
      if replace
      then ok time
      else if existing < time
           then ok existing
           else ok time
    with_slot q k (some v)
enqueue.upstream_note: EventQueue::enqueue; overflow is structurally impossible, so no Result

Inv.code:
/-- The reachability invariant: the next poll is always scheduled within 30 s
(and at least 1 s). Because it is a fact about `next_poll_interval` for any
failure count, it holds of every state. -/
def Inv (q : Queue) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, next_poll_interval q.fail_count = ok r → 1 ≤ r.val ∧ r.val ≤ 30
